html:
A large mosque in Touba, Senegal, built over the tomb of Amadou Bamba and inaugurated in 1963, one of the largest mosques in Africa.

Building began in the 1930s, paid for by the gifts of Mouride disciples, many of them groundnut farmers. Touba is run by the brotherhood's leader, the khalife, with its own rules. Each year the Grand Magal draws millions of pilgrims, making Touba the scene of the largest gathering in West Africa. The city has grown from a village into the second largest in Senegal. Like the old mosques of Timbuktu, it stands for the strength of Sufi orders in West African Islam.
sum: A large mosque in Touba, Senegal, built over the tomb of Amadou Bamba and inaugurated in 1963, one of the largest mosques in Africa.
